skill.name: create-plan
skill.description: Create concise, scoped implementation plans for coding tasks when a user explicitly asks for a plan.
skill.summary: Turn coding requests into clear plans with scope, ordered actions, validation steps, and open questions.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in SKILL.md. I found no evidence of executable code, command execution, data exfiltration, prompt injection, or other semantic security issues.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses Markdown inline backticks around documentation paths such as README.md and docs/. It is instructional prose, not Ruby or shell execution.
Lines 42-63 are a fenced Markdown template showing the desired plan format. The backticks delimit a documentation block and are not executed.

content.value_statement: Coding requests can become unclear when scope, validation, and risks are not separated. This skill produces a concise plan with ordered actions, scope boundaries, tests, and open questions.
actual_capabilities: Scans repository context and obvious documentation before planning.
Identifies relevant files, frameworks, commands, and constraints.
Asks one or two follow-up questions only when planning is blocked.
Produces a single plan with scope, ordered action items, and open questions.
Includes validation, testing, edge cases, and rollout considerations when relevant.
Keeps plans implementation-agnostic and avoids writing code snippets.
limitations: It is designed for coding tasks, not general project management.
It does not edit files or implement the plan.
It does not run tests or verify code behavior directly.
Plan quality depends on the available repository context.

use_cases.title: Plan a Bug Fix
use_cases.description: Convert a bug report into a scoped repair plan with likely files, validation steps, and edge cases.

use_cases.title: Scope a Feature
use_cases.description: Break a requested feature into ordered implementation tasks before making code changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactor
use_cases.description: Map a risky refactor into discovery, change, test, and rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple task plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for adding a small coding change. Include scope, ordered action items, validation, and any open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan from a Bug Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request based on observed behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan to investigate and fix this bug: [describe the bug]. Include likely files to inspect, tests to add, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature Across Modules
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a multi-area feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for implementing [feature] across this repository. Separate in-scope and out-of-scope work, then list ordered tasks and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Risky Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with migration or rollout risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for refactoring [area]. Include discovery, compatibility risks, migration steps, tests, rollout, rollback, and open questions.

output_examples.input: Create a plan to add pagination to the issues list.
output_examples.output: A concise plan with scope, ordered discovery and implementation tasks, validation steps for page boundaries, and one open question about default page size.

output_examples.input: Plan a refactor of the authentication service.
output: Scope separates service internals from unrelated login UI changes.
Action items cover current behavior mapping, interface changes, tests, rollout, and rollback.
Open questions identify compatibility requirements and migration timing.

best_practices: Use the skill before implementation when the task has unclear scope.
Provide the bug report, feature request, or repository area to anchor the plan.
Review open questions before asking the assistant to implement the plan.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when you want immediate code edits instead of planning.
Do not expect it to validate behavior without running tools or tests.
Do not use it for non-coding work that needs a different planning format.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: No. It operates in read-only mode and returns a plan only.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you explicitly want a concise plan for a coding task before implementation.

faq.question: Can it ask follow-up questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks one or two questions only when missing information blocks responsible planning.

faq.question: What format does it produce?
faq.answer: It produces a short plan with scope, action items, validation steps, risks, and open questions when needed.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it replace project management tools?
faq.answer: No. It creates implementation plans for individual coding tasks, not full project tracking systems.
